cur:catacombs-santa-maria-antiqua-sarcop.summary: This tub-shaped sarcophagus unfolds from left to right: a ship and Jonah cast up by the sea-monster, Jonah resting, a praying woman, a seated philosopher reading, the Good Shepherd, and the Baptism of a small naked Christ, closing with fishermen casting a net. It is one of the earliest sarcophagi to tell the Christian story, combining the old pastoral images with a Gospel scene.
facts: The Commons description lists the scenes as ship, Jonah, sheep, orans, seated man with a scroll, Christ the Good Shepherd, the Baptism of Christ and two fishermen (perhaps Peter and Andrew).
Commons dates it to about 275, which would make it earlier than the Peace of the Church.
cur:catacombs-santa-maria-antiqua-sarcop.notes: The identification of the baptism as Christ's own is generally accepted but not certain.

cur:catacombs-arles-susanna.summary: A central medallion with a couple's portraits divides two registers of crowded scenes, among them the story of Susanna, from which the sarcophagus is named, and miracles of Christ. Susanna, saved from false accusation, and the healed and raised of the Gospels speak together of God's deliverance.
facts: The museum states that it is carved from Carrara marble and represents the story of chaste Susanna.

cur:objects2-castledermot-south-cross.summary: At the centre of the west face of the South Cross the crucified Christ is flanked by David playing the harp and the Sacrifice of Isaac, the Old Testament type of his offering. Below, the shaft shows the hermits Paul and Anthony fed by the raven, Adam and Eve, the Temptation of Saint Anthony and Daniel in the lions' den, and a hunting scene on the base.
facts: The pairing of the Crucifixion with the Sacrifice of Isaac expresses the early Christian reading of Isaac as a figure of Christ.
cur:objects2-castledermot-south-cross.notes: Scene identifications from the photographer's Commons description.

walters:48.2086.5.summary: Like an emperor among his officials, Christ, named IC XC, sits enthroned and faces the viewer, blessing with one hand and holding a jewelled Gospel book in the other. The archangels Michael and Gabriel stand at either side in Byzantine court dress, the one at the left holding a staff. Even in its broken state the glazed tile keeps the warm browns, greens and golds that once made it shine on a church furnishing.
facts: The Walters notes that, although its origin is unknown, the tile is very similar to tiles known to have been made in Constantinople.
It was bought in Istanbul around 1950 and acquired by the museum in 1956.
